trap_description: Using random UUIDv4 as clustered primary key in PostgreSQL/MySQL, causing massive B-tree page splits and write amplification
bad_example: id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid() on tables with >1M rows
remediation_rule: Use time-sortable UUIDv7 or ULID; preserves natural temporal insertion order and compact B-tree leaf filling.

trap_description: Adding boolean is_deleted flag without partial indexes, causing full table scans and breaking UNIQUE constraints
bad_example: is_deleted BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE; UNIQUE(email) fails if previous user is soft-deleted
remediation_rule: Use deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL and partial index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON users (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL.

trap_description: Using native CREATE TYPE enum in PostgreSQL for application workflow states that evolve over time
bad_example: CREATE TYPE status_enum AS ENUM ('DRAFT', 'ACTIVE'); Adding new values requires exclusive locks.
remediation_rule: Store as plain VARCHAR/TEXT with application-level validation; allows rolling deploys with new and old versions running concurrently.

trap_description: Creating FOREIGN KEY constraints without an index on the referencing child column
bad_example: orders.user_id REFERENCES users(id) without CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_id
remediation_rule: Always create an index on every foreign key column to prevent full table scans and share locks during parent row deletion.

trap_description: Executing queries filtering on JSONB fields without GIN or functional expression indexes
bad_example: SELECT * FROM events WHERE payload->>'event_type' = 'CLICK'; (triggers Seq Scan)
remediation_rule: Add GIN index: USING GIN (payload jsonb_path_ops) or expression index: CREATE INDEX ON events ((payload->>'event_type')).

trap_description: Fetching parent entities and lazily issuing an individual SELECT query for each child relation in a loop
bad_example: orders = Repo.list(); for o in orders: o.items = Repo.get_items(o.id)
remediation_rule: Use eager loading (JOIN FETCH, selectinload, or include) to batch fetch child records in a single query.
